exposure: Gestational age at delivery: Group 1 (≤27(+ 6) weeks), Group 2 (28-33(+ 6) weeks), Group 3 (34-36(+ 6) weeks), and Group 4 (≥37 weeks)
cohort: 2516 singleton pregnant women with severe preeclampsia in mainland China
finding: Although cesarean section was associated with a lower perinatal mortality rate in pregnant women with severe preeclampsia, it did not affect the rate of maternal postpartum hemorrhage or mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a lower perinatal mortality rate but a higher neonatal asphyxia rate in the 28-33(+ 6) weeks gestation group compared to vaginal delivery.
gest_age: Varied, categorized into four groups: ≤27(+ 6) weeks, 28-33(+ 6) weeks, 34-36(+ 6) weeks, and ≥37 weeks
